chargeMentale.q1: Who notices something is about to run out before it actually does?
chargeMentale.q2: Who decides what you are going to eat this week?
chargeMentale.q3: Who keeps track of what is left in the cupboards when you go shopping?
chargeMentale.q4: Who notices when the sheets, towels or tea towels need changing?
chargeMentale.q5: Who thinks through everything that needs sorting before having someone over for dinner?
chargeMentale.q6: Who remembers to book medical appointments, for both of you?
chargeMentale.q7: Who notices when something is broken or worn out and will need dealing with?
chargeMentale.q8: Who keeps track of deadlines for the car, the home and the appliances?
chargeMentale.q9: Who thinks about the clothes that will need buying before the next season?
chargeMentale.q10: Who knows where the things you only take out twice a year are kept?
chargeMentale.q11: Who opens the post and knows what is in it?
chargeMentale.q12: Who keeps track of payment dates, subscriptions and direct debits?
chargeMentale.q13: Who deals with the tedious admin whenever there is some to do?
chargeMentale.q14: Who has a clear idea of what is left in the account at the end of the month?
chargeMentale.q15: Who thinks to compare, cancel or renegotiate when a contract gets too expensive?
chargeMentale.q16: Who remembers birthdays, on both sides of the family?
chargeMentale.q17: Who thinks about presents, chooses them and buys them?
chargeMentale.q18: Who takes the initiative to call or invite the families?
chargeMentale.q19: Who organises the holidays, from picking the dates to booking?
chargeMentale.q20: Who notices first when something is wrong with the other one?
chargeMentale.desaccordsIntro: You gave different answers on {{n}} of the 20 tasks. Here are the three where the gap is widest, and they are exactly the ones worth talking about.
chargeMentale.v_equipe_t: You are a team, and you both know it
chargeMentale.v_equipe_d: The load is split roughly evenly, and more importantly you are describing the same thing. That is rarer than it sounds: in most couples, even where the split is fair, each person substantially overestimates their own share. Here your two snapshots line up, which means you have already had this conversation, or you never needed to.
chargeMentale.v_equipe_a: There is nothing to fix. The only thing to watch is what comes next: a move, a child, a change of job redistributes everything, and the current balance does not survive those moments on its own. Retake this test after the next one.
chargeMentale.v_flou_t: Evenly split, but neither of you sees the same thing
chargeMentale.v_flou_d: The total is balanced, and yet you are not describing the same daily life. Each of you has a precise view of what you carry and a vague view of what the other carries: that is how attention normally works, you see what you do and not what gets done without you. The risk here is not unfairness, it is resentment built on a misunderstanding.
chargeMentale.v_flou_a: Take your three biggest disagreements and, for each one, describe concretely what you do: at what point, how often, and what has to be held in mind beforehand. Nine times out of ten the conversation ends with « I had no idea you did that », on both sides.
chargeMentale.v_assume_t: The imbalance is real, and both of you can see it
chargeMentale.v_assume_d: One of you carries clearly more, and you agree on that. This is a far healthier situation than it looks, because nothing is being denied: the imbalance is on the table, so it can be discussed and corrected. What remains to be established is whether it is chosen, for a good reason and for a set period, or simply settled in.
chargeMentale.v_assume_a: The question is not « is this fair » but « does this hold ». An unequal split, agreed on during a hard period, is sustainable. The same one, with no end date and never actually decided by anyone, ends up costing a great deal. Set a date to revisit it, not an intention.
chargeMentale.v_invisible_t: One of you carries it, and the other cannot see it
chargeMentale.v_invisible_d: This is the result this test exists for, and it is the most common one. The load is clearly carried by one person, and your two sets of answers do not tell the same story: the one carrying it knows, the other believes it is more shared than that. It is almost never bad faith. The mental load is made of things that only become visible the moment they stop being done, and as long as they are being done, nobody else notices them.
chargeMentale.v_invisible_a: Do not start with a list of grievances, it never works. Take the three disagreements above, one at a time, and have each of you describe what they think the other does. It is the gap between the two accounts that makes the thing visible, far better than any demonstration. Then transfer whole areas, including the remembering: delegating the doing while keeping the reminding relieves nobody.
chargeMentale.v_soloEquilibre_t: You are describing a shared load
chargeMentale.v_soloEquilibre_d: Based on your answers, the invisible organising of daily life is split roughly evenly between you. That is good news, with one important caveat: this result reflects your point of view only. And this is precisely the point on which the two members of a couple diverge most.
chargeMentale.v_soloEquilibre_a: Have your partner take the test separately, then compare. If your two results look alike, the balance is real. If they diverge sharply, it is not the split that needs revisiting first, it is the conversation you have not had yet.
chargeMentale.v_soloDesequilibre_t: You are describing a load resting mainly on one person
chargeMentale.v_soloDesequilibre_d: Your answers show a clear imbalance: most of what has to be anticipated, remembered and organised rests on the same shoulders. This kind of imbalance rarely arrives by decision, it settles in on its own, one task at a time, because whoever notices first ends up handling it, and because once it has become their area nobody else thinks about it any more.
chargeMentale.v_soloDesequilibre_a: The natural reflex is to ask for help. That is exactly what does not work: asking for help means keeping the job of knowing what needs doing and when. The only transfer that genuinely lightens the load is a whole area, including the remembering. And to make the case, have your partner take the test: the gap between your two results will say it better than you can.
chargeMentale.modesDesc: The same twenty tasks either way! Only the result the test can give you at the end is different.
chargeMentale.modeSoloDesc: You answer on your own, about your relationship
chargeMentale.modeDuoDesc: You each take a turn, on the same phone
